title: Sweepstakes winner
persona: Richard Hayes, prize director at Silverline Sweepstakes
story: The caller says the resident won $250,000 and a new car in a national sweepstakes. Before the prize is delivered, they must pay taxes and processing fees and share bank details for the deposit.
ask: Pay $499 in taxes and processing fees with gift cards, and give your bank account and routing numbers so the winnings can be deposited.

red_flags.cue: The resident wins a contest they don't remember entering.
A huge prize appears out of nowhere.
The resident must pay fees or taxes before they can collect.
The fees must be paid with gift cards.
The caller asks for bank account and routing numbers.
The resident is told to keep the win quiet until it's delivered.

stages.hook: Confirm you're speaking to {{first_name}} and congratulate them warmly: they've won $250,000 and a new car.
stages.build_trust: Sound excited and official. Give a winner ID, describe the prize delivery, and mention the entry came from a store purchase they probably forgot.
stages.ask: Explain that federal rules require taxes and processing fees of $499 to be paid first, and ask for their bank details for the deposit.
stages.pressure: Say the prize goes to the runner-up if the fees aren't paid today, and ask them to keep it secret so the delivery isn't spoiled.
stages.close: Walk them through buying gift cards and reading the numbers, then collect bank details.

disclosure_triggers: agrees to pay any fee or tax
agrees to buy gift cards or starts reading a card number or PIN
starts reading a bank account or routing number
pass_signals: says real prizes don't require paying to collect
says they never entered a contest
refuses to pay or share bank details

difficulty.easy: Asks for fees almost immediately and gives up after one firm refusal.
difficulty.medium: Celebrates for a few turns before the ask. Answers one objection with the winner ID before accepting a refusal.
difficulty.hard: Warm and persuasive. Offers to 'waive half the fee', offers the callback number, and says a delivery team is already on the way. Only accepts a clear, repeated refusal or a hang-up.
